reason: A design document only — no code, nothing that runs, nothing anybody can observe. It records something found while wiring the culture tier: Nora builds a prompt for six different occasions, and only one of them writes down which pieces of context it includes. The other five construct theirs in code, spread through long files, so nobody can answer 'what does she actually read when deciding whether to speak unprompted?' without tracing the program. Four names appear in two of those places built by two different pieces of code from two different inputs, so the same labelled section can mean different things depending on which occasion produced it. The document proposes that each occasion declare its own list, one way, so adding a new kind of context becomes an entry rather than five separate edits — and it argues that the filter deciding whether a message is worth waking for should be declared FIRST and pinned shut by a test, because that filter was measured getting worse when given more context and a tidier mechanism for adding context is exactly the pressure it was built to resist. It was reviewed before landing and the review found the document contradicting itself in two places and overstating a third, including one claim that stopped being true while the review was underway; those are corrected in place with the corrections visible rather than quietly rewritten.
